findings.reason: the negative control as written cannot fail for the very regression it is meant to catch, so a worker applying it sees a green test and either reports a false blocker or closes the section believing a guard that still guards nothing; the plan needs the control to force the branch where an XDG literal diverges (drop `.config/reckon` so the legacy `~/docs-server` branch is active, or add a legacy-layout case).
findings.text: the done-when's first control, "the test fails when `_guard_store()` returns a path literal", is false for the path literal §16 existed to remove: because §20's test sets HOME to a temporary directory and creates `.config/reckon` under it, `_config_home()` takes its XDG branch, so a guard that hardcodes `Path.home() / ".config" / "reckon"` returns exactly the expectation and the test passes. Measured: with HOME=home1 (containing .config/reckon) and RECKON_HOME=home2, `real_store_home()` == home1/.config/reckon, and a call-time XDG literal `Path.home()/".config"/"reckon"` also == home1/.config/reckon, so equal; only a literal evaluated at import against the unpatched HOME differs. A guard regressing to the XDG literal — the pre-§16 defect, which §16's commit message says "only matches the XDG layout" — would therefore survive §20's test.
